finding: BR-076 bounds a claim with ten stale leases at twenty git calls of 30 seconds each and nine waits. next-id limits every git call of a claim: git init, then fetch, rev-parse, show, mktree, commit-tree, and push per try, so the worst case is 61 calls. Count all 61, or state the bound for the twenty calls that reach the remote.
why_this_severity: Each call still stops at 30 seconds, so a claim always ends with a named cause, as QS-20 requires (no to fails_purpose); a reader who plans a timeout from the stated bound gets a third of the real worst case (raises_cost).

finding: The rows Writes and Seed output of the next-id contract call CID-G06 and CID-G03 open. The code answers both: seed runs in a throwaway repository (next-id:390), and its output holds the start and pair lines without the token (next-id:402). State both answers, or ask the stakeholder first.
why_this_severity: Both answers are the safe reading of the proposal, and a caller can use the seed either way (no to fails_purpose); a test writer reads the two rows as open and skips the checks, as the QA strategy does for CID-01-IT-06 (raises_cost).

finding: 37 of the 39 test rows say planned although their tests exist; the CID-10 rows name a file whose tests carry no CID marker; line 122 says 'for all ten prefixes'. Set each built test to implemented, name the three init-factory tests, and say twelve prefixes. CID-11-AC-01 stays planned.
why_this_severity: The tests exist and run in the suite, so coverage is as planned (no to fails_purpose); a reader must search tests/factory/ to learn which rows are built (raises_cost).

finding: The case table of next-id --move-to-origin starts from a set agent-factory.counterRemote, a present origin, and a local claim commit. It names no result when the setting is missing, origin is missing, the local repository holds no refs/ids/counters, or the local counter already holds a marker commit. The second case is real: a User who declines the seed keeps the setting (CIF-G06), adds origin later, and VIRGIL offers the move by BR-106. Add one row per case with its exit code and message, and the matching event to the Move Lifecycle. Owner: domain-modeling-agent.
why_this_severity: Every case can end with a non-zero exit and a message that changes nothing, which an implementer can pick from the Failure row (no to fails_purpose); the implementer and the test writer must still invent the four messages, and the Move Lifecycle has no event for them (raises_cost).

finding: BR-102 and the Move Lifecycle restart the move after every stale lease on C and state no limit. The claim stops after ten stale leases (BR-072). Only the QA strategy raises the question (CIF-QG01); the gaps report has no gap for it. Record the open limit as a gap of the gaps report, so the planner asks the stakeholder, and cite it in BR-102.
why_this_severity: Claims on a local counter are rare while a person runs the move, so the move ends in practice (no to fails_purpose); a reader of BR-102 sees no open question, and the planner finds it only in the QA strategy (raises_cost).

finding: BR-102 says the move exits non-zero when the push fails, and in the same rule says gap CIF-G08 asks for the exit codes. The contract of next-id --move-to-origin and the REFUSED state of the Move Lifecycle also take non-zero. The gaps report (CIF-G08, CIF-C07) and the QA strategy (CIF-11-IT-01, CIF-11-IT-02) treat the code as open and leave it unasserted. Decide in one place: either non-zero follows from the Failure row of next-id and CIF-G08 closes, or the three structure files mark the code as open. Owner: domain-modeling-agent.
why_this_severity: Every reading leads to a non-zero exit, so an implementer can act (no to fails_purpose); the test writer leaves the code unasserted although three files state it (raises_cost).

finding: The Writes row of next-id still says that a claim leaves the clone unchanged (BR-075). finding: The contract of next-id --plan-seed puts the seed command on standard output and names no stream for the warnings of BR-100 or for the message that the counter is in use. VIRGIL reads the command from the output, and the Output row says one line. A warning on standard output breaks that line. Name the stream of each: for example, the warnings on standard error, and the in-use message on standard output.
why_this_severity: An implementer can follow the Failure row and send messages to standard error (no to fails_purpose); the CIF-06 tests must still guess where to read the warning (raises_cost).

finding: BR-099 counts only the strict names backlog/ST-NNNN.md and docs/findings/<PREFIX>-NNNN.md and a heading ## T-NNNN. BR-100 counts any name that starts with a prefix, a hyphen, and digits, such as SPEC-011-title.md. By BR-100, the ADR files docs/adr/NNNN-*.md start with digits and do not count. The todo headings of this project carry a title, such as ## T-0020 — A claim can still open a credential dialog. Let BR-099 name the three locations and BR-100 the match for backlog and findings, state that ADR files match NNNN-*.md, and state that a todo heading counts when it starts with ## T-NNNN. Owner: domain-modeling-agent.
why_this_severity: The Scenarios of CIF-05 and CIF-06 show the intended match, so an implementer can act (no to fails_purpose); a reader must combine two rules that each read as the whole match (raises_cost).

finding: --plan-seed reads the IDs on each branch. The commit that fixes a minor finding deletes its register line (glossary, Register Line). When that line held the highest ID of a prefix, no branch tip holds it, and the seed hands the number out again. State whether the mode reads the branch tips or the history of docs/findings/register/, or record the reuse as an accepted limit next to CIF-G10.
why_this_severity: The case needs a fixed minor finding with the highest ID of its prefix before the first seed, which is rare (no to fails_purpose); a reused ID then points to two findings in old review reports, and a reader has to tell them apart (raises_cost).

finding: Three Factory files write T IDs into docs/spec/work/todos.md, not todo.md: playbooks/architecture-review.md appends T-$(date +%s)-001 entries, agents/coaching-agent.md files T-NNN entries, and playbooks/brownfield-onboarding.md documents debt there. BR-107 makes only todo.md writers T producers, and BR-099 does not read todos.md. So these files keep numbering T outside next-id. T-0008 tracks the merge of the two lists. Name todos.md and its writers as out of scope with a reference to T-0008, or add them to the scope.
why_this_severity: The IDs in todos.md use other forms than T-NNNN, so they do not collide with the counter in this project (no to fails_purpose); a planner cannot tell from the specification whether these files are forgotten or left out on purpose (raises_cost).

finding: The glossary lists tag under Avoid for ID Prefix.
